card.name: Words before keep-available or kept-on-hand instructions
card.fires_on: Words just before a verb of having, keeping or storing something on hand, such as the end of 'resuscitation' or 'agonist', or 'Keep a' and 'syringe and'. Seen mostly in warnings and instructions in drug labels.

modes.label: Resuscitation and agonist endings
modes.description: Final piece of 'resuscitation' or 'agonist' in advice to have equipment or a rescue drug ready.
modes.example: Always have cardiopulmonary resusc<<itation>> personnel and equipment readily available and monitor patients

modes.label: Keep or store instructions
modes.description: Small words in phrases about keeping or storing something for later use.
modes.example: Keep<< a>> diary to remember where your last shot was

modes.label: Linking word before a verb
modes.description: A linking word or noun that leads into a verb describing what something does or allows.
modes.example: This<< allows>> the Leonardo to appear to a connected computer

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning 'needs' or 'provided' and away from words meaning holds, stores or keeps.
card.plain: It fires on words in instructions to have or keep something ready, such as resuscitation gear or a rescue inhaler.
